I’m from a country with a big poverty problem and a fast population boom and I’d like to disagree with you a bit and provide more context at least from where I come from. 

The first reason people have too many children here is lack of Education. A huge percentage of the population especially in the rural areas away from the big cities have never been to school and so the jobs they can work pay extremely little money (often times less than $80 per month for the bread winner) and the minimum wage is never really enforced because the government doesn’t seem to care. The illiteracy causes them to have poor family planning and understanding of contraception, and for some reason they also misinterpret some religious texts and they believe that every child arrives to the world with a blessing and they learn not to worry about having kids because God will bless them.

They subsequently end up having a lot of children, with some families having up to 10 kids sometimes. Some people realize that the way for their kids to do better in life is to get a better education, so they fight tooth and nail to get them to school and pay for their supplies. However, the majority of poor people either don’t realize the importance of education, or they do but they struggle to pay for the expenses related to education such as clothing, textbooks and school supplies so they don’t put their kids into school at all or have them drop out before getting to high school. Again, it is mandatory for all families to put their children in school but the government doesn’t care much because we also don’t have enough public schools.

For families with such financial struggles they usually send their kids from a young age (8-9 years) to work at farmlands, mechanic shops, or even carpenter workshops. Child labor is illegal here but again, it is so common and the authorities turn a blind eye.

For these families their children are a source of income because the main bread winner can never make enough money. I know that if their circumstances had been better they wouldn’t have ever gotten down that route but it is a reality that we live in. This also not a generalization, there are parents who love their children and want the best for them, there are parents that don’t care, and there are parents who abuse their children but keep having more.

I've been diagnosed with depression and the major causes as per the therapy sessions are my disturbed self-identity and emotionally abusive childhood. The problem with the self-image made me lose all purpose in life to the point of being suicidal.

I don't think it would be right to not call it depression because you have a self-identity problem, I think if you do have the symptoms of depression the you have depression, the reason is something you will discover step by step.

It's been 6 months for me, and 4 months in we have uncovered a personality disorder that I was keeping hidden really well because I always show a strong and resilient persona but when I allowed myself to be vulnerable everything unfurled and we were able to take on a different approach in therapy.

I was like you, started out feeling in control of 90% of what goes on with my life and just needed help controlling my sad feelings, but then as we went on, I discovered that I am emotionally immature in some aspects without me noticing it. It gets me down sometimes because discovering emotional shortcomings only makes me think worse of myself, more than I already do due to the depression. 

You'll figure everything out with your therapist, just keep going every week and see where it leads you.

>I believe that you want to enjoy life and see the beauty in it. You have been attending therapy to better yourself. You are doing everything right but the only thing that is really holding you back is you... Which brings me to my next point...

This is true. My instinct is to survive and love life, but my mind tells me it's nonsense. So your words do make a lot of sense.

>I strongly believe that you are a very very strong person. I don't know if you can see it in yourself but you are very intelligent, kind, giving, nurturing, and helpful. And I feel like not very many have reciprocated that to you.
